selected_goal_name: Mana Resource System (Pool, Spend, Post-Cast Regen)
selected_goal_description: Implement a reusable Mana component (max/current mana, Spend(amount), regeneration that resumes after a fixed post-cast delay), mirroring the existing PlayerHealth pattern, ready for the three required spells (Charged Fireball, Frost Field, Force Wave) to consume.
implementation_summary: Added a PlayerMana MonoBehaviour (Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scripts/PlayerMana.cs) mirroring PlayerHealth's structure: MaxMana/CurrentMana properties, a bool Spend(float) that fails and leaves the pool unchanged when insufficient, a public Tick(deltaTime) driven from Update (also directly callable from tests, mirroring DoorInteractable.Tick), and Update-driven regen that only resumes once postCastRegenDelay seconds have elapsed since the last successful spend. Added DebugManaSpendControl.cs mirroring DebugDamageControl's debug-trigger pattern (L key by default) to exercise Spend() without any spell existing yet. Added PlayerManaUI.cs mirroring DoorInteractionUI's progress-fill binding (fillAmount = CurrentMana/MaxMana). Wired all three into DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs: the Player gets PlayerMana + DebugManaSpendControl components, and BuildUI now also builds a ManaFill bar (Image.Type.Filled, same background+fill pattern as the door's ProgressFill, positioned lower on screen so it never overlaps) plus a stacked "DEBUG: Spend Mana (L)" button, and the ControlsHud text now documents the L key. No spell-casting logic was added — Spend is only exercised via the debug trigger, matching the candidate's stated implementation_scope exactly.

manual_unity_validation: Open the project in Unity 6000.1.8f1, let it import the new scripts (no compile errors expected).
Run No Safe Circle > Build Door Prototype Scene from the menu to regenerate DoorPrototype.unity with the new Player mana components and UI wired in.
Enter Play Mode: confirm a blue ManaFill bar appears near the bottom-center of the screen, starting full.

Click the 'DEBUG: Spend Mana (L)' button (or press L) repeatedly and confirm CurrentMana drops by 25 each time (button greys out functionally once mana is insufficient, i.e. clicks stop reducing the bar) and Spend refuses below zero.
After spending, confirm the mana bar stays flat for ~2 seconds (postCastRegenDelay) before refilling; confirm spending again during the refill resets the delay.
Run the Unity Test Runner (Play Mode) and confirm the 5 new PlayerManaPlayModeTests pass alongside the existing DoorInteractionPlayModeTests and DoorPrototypeSceneBuilderTests (Edit Mode).
requirements_satisfied: Reusable PlayerMana component with MaxMana/CurrentMana pool, mirroring PlayerHealth's field/property/Awake pattern.
Spend(float) method that returns success/failure and leaves the pool unchanged on failure.
Regeneration resumes only after a fixed, configurable post-cast delay elapses since the last spend, and any new spend resets that delay.
Update-driven regen loop with a public Tick(deltaTime) for deterministic Play Mode testing, mirroring DoorInteractable's Tick pattern.
Minimal UI hookup (ManaFill bar bound via PlayerManaUI) mirroring DoorInteractionUI's progress-fill Image.Type.Filled pattern.
Debug 'Spend Mana' trigger (DebugManaSpendControl, key L) mirroring DebugDamageControl, sufficient to test the pool standalone with no spell-casting logic included.
No spell-casting logic (Fireball/Frost Field/Force Wave) was implemented — scope stayed to the mana pool only.
remaining_work: None for the selected goal itself. The three spells (Charged Fireball, Frost Field, Force Wave) that will call PlayerMana.Spend() are separate, out-of-scope future goals per the contract.
Human/Unity verification of the generated scene and UI layout (bar visibility, button wiring, HUD text) since no Unity executable was available in this container to run it.
